meta.title: Mongolian Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 2357 phrases and sentences · 29 phrases, 2328 sentences · both directions
meta.desc: Mongolian said whole: greetings and leave-takings, courtesies, the phrasebook questions a visitor needs, the weather, exclamations, a proverb, an idiom and the calls a herder makes to the animals, then a set of short everyday sentences. Both study directions, each a card of its own: Mongolian → English and English → Mongolian. 29 PHRASES are every phrase, interjection and proverb English Wiktionary has for Mongolian that the level decks do not teach (vulgar ones and mere sounds left out), with Wiktionary's own meaning and its 'formal' or 'informal': сайн уу 'hello' (informal; A1 teaches the formal сайн байна уу), өглөөний мэнд 'good morning', тавтай морилогтун 'welcome', сайн яваарай 'bon voyage', гялайлаа 'thank you' (formal), сайхан хооллоорой 'enjoy your meal', the proverb овоо босгоогүй бол шаазгай хаанаас суух вэ, given by Wiktionary as 'it takes two to tango', and the idiom нэг сумаар хоёр туулай буудах 'to kill two birds with one stone'. 2328 SENTENCES are Tatoeba's short Mongolian sentences (eight words at most) with their English translation, printed as Tatoeba has them, each card giving the sentence's Tatoeba number. Mongolian has a familiar and a polite 'you' (чи, та), so where two sentences share an English one the card says which is which. Tatoeba's stock name Tom (Том) is in many of them. Nothing here is invented, and nothing the level decks teach is repeated. It is not a CEFR level. There is no speaker button: few devices have a Mongolian voice. Sources: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0); Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
